title: Sarvam AI API Pricing: Per-Token Rates (2026 Guide)
summary: Sarvam AI API pricing provides per-million-token rates for each chat model. Compare costs across models to find which suits your budget best.
body_markdown:
## Fix the overrun with Activepieces


If a small workflow logs every Sarvam AI call, totals the day's spend, alerts at 50% and 80% of budget, and pauses the job at the cap, a runaway loop stops itself instead of showing up on next month's invoice.


Sarvam AI's prices stay exactly as listed; this only limits how much of them you can consume.


Do the generic fixes first, because they work without any extra tool:


- Set whatever usage or rate limit the provider's dashboard allows, so the vendor refuses work past a ceiling you chose.
- Cap retries in code, so one failing request can't quietly become many billed ones.
- Turn on budget alerts wherever the account offers them, so a person hears about drift before the invoice.
- Keep a daily total of your own, because the provider's figure arrives after the spending and yours arrives with it.


Because each covers a gap the others leave, no single rule is enough. Provider limits are coarse, retry caps do nothing about legitimate volume, and alerts alone only inform.


### Configure spending alerts and pause automation


To follow the fourth rule without writing a service, use Activepieces, an open-source AI automation platform that lets you wire the log, the total and the stop.


Starting at a trigger, the flow below calls Sarvam AI through an HTTP step, and adds the call's cost to a daily-total step. It then branches into a 50% alert, an 80% alert and a pause step at the cap.


The retry limit of 3 sits on the HTTP step, so a failing call is billed at most a few times, not indefinitely.


The job that hammered Sarvam at 02:10 was an agent-shaped script with a key and nobody answerable for it: code has no tenant, no role and no audit trail of its own.


Activepieces treats agents as actors too, giving each its own least-privilege access, alongside custom RBAC, SSO and SCIM for people and control over which apps a team may connect.


Every tool call it makes is logged separately with its own input and output, which means a retry loop shows up as 40 distinct calls rather than one opaque result. MoneyGram, Moneypenny, Alan and FundingSocieties run it in production.


The two alert branches matter for different reasons. The 50% message is a planning signal, telling you whether the day's volume matches the budget you built from the price table.


The 80% message is a warning that gives someone time to act before the pause fires.


Once the screenshot's flow is running, the remaining work is calibration. Set the cap from your real monthly budget divided across days, then review the alert history to see whether the thresholds fire too early or too late.
